name: Honduras
snapshot: Nasry Asfura, endorsed by Trump days before the vote, took office in January 2026 after a disputed count returned the National Party to power.
culture: Honduras is home to the Maya ruins of Copán, famous for their carved stelae, and to Garifuna and Miskito communities on the Caribbean coast. Baleadas, flour tortillas with beans and cream, are the national street food. Football is followed passionately; a 1969 match helped spark a short war with El Salvador.
society: Honduras has struggled with some of the world's highest murder rates, driven by gangs and drug trafficking, though they have fallen. Remittances from the US are about a quarter of GDP. Garment factories and coffee are key exports. Former president Juan Orlando Hernández was convicted of drug trafficking in New York in 2024 and pardoned by Trump in 2025.

story: Honduras has one of the most turbulent democracies in the Americas: a coup in 2009 against President Manuel Zelaya, a disputed election in 2017, and a former president, Juan Orlando Hernández, convicted in New York in 2024 of helping traffic more than 400 tonnes of cocaine. In 2022 Zelaya's wife Xiomara Castro became the first woman president on a leftist platform. The 2025 election to replace her became one of the most contested in the region's recent history, and Washington put its thumb on the scale.

Days before the 30 November vote, Trump endorsed Nasry "Tito" Asfura, a construction magnate and former Tegucigalpa mayor from Hernández's National Party, and attacked the rival candidates; he also pardoned Hernández. Counting took nearly a month. Asfura was declared the winner with 40.27 percent to 39.53 percent for TV personality Salvador Nasralla of the Liberal Party, a margin of fewer than 30,000 votes out of 3.7 million (AP via News4Jax). Castro's party, Libre, came a distant third with about 19 percent (El Nuevo Diario). Both Nasralla and Libre alleged fraud, and Nasralla still says he is the rightful president. Asfura took office on 27 January in a deliberately austere ceremony in Congress, without foreign heads of state, promising to shrink the state and "confront insecurity head-on." As one analyst noted, all three major parties have been credibly linked to drug money (World Politics Review).
briefing.power: A presidential republic. The president is directly elected for a single four-year term by simple plurality; the 128-seat National Congress is elected at the same time.
briefing.holders: President Nasry Asfura (National Party), since 27 January 2026.
